newsitem.title: THAILAND: GF says unhurt by loans to property sector.
newsitem.headline: GF says unhurt by loans to property sector.

text.p: General Finance and Securities Plc (GF) on Tuesday dismissed concern that its 40 percent loan exposure to the ailing Thai property sector would put the company in financial trouble.
GF chairman Suchartchan Pravit said most of its large property loans are protected by sufficient collateral.

He said about seven percent of the firm's outstanding 55 billion baht ($2.12 billion) loans are non-performing, including 1.6 billion baht of sub-standard assets and 1.7 billion baht of doubtful loans.
Most finance companies extend about one quarter of all their loans to the property sector which has faced a four-year slump with no immediate recovery in sight, analysts say.
Suchartchan said GF has not been affected by a recent central bank instruction for finance companies to set aside additional 20 percent provisions for sub-standard assets.
He said his company had met the higher reserve level before the government decision.
Suchartchan said only about seven percent of GF's total lending were margin loans extended to retail stock investors against a 13-14 percent average for the industry.
The banker denied local media reports and said the eight companies within the GF group have no plan to merge in near or medium term.
GF closed steady at 18.50 baht on Tuesday after its weak performance in the past two weeks and against 28.00 baht at end-February.
